title: Identification of epigenetic readers by DAPPL
protocol: Mix 1.7 g yeast nitrogen base without amino acids, 5 g ammonium sulfate, 20 g glucose, 2 g amino acid dropout mixes, and 20 g agar into 1 L ddH₂O.
Autoclave the medium at 121°C for 15 minutes.
Pour ~20 mL of SC-Ura/glucose agar per 10 cm polystyrene Petri dish.
Take out 10 μl of each human ORF expression yeast clone and draw it on the SC-Ura/glucose plates.
Put the plates in a 30°C incubator for 48 hours.
Transfer each of the yeast clones to 800 µL of SC-Ura/glucose liquid medium in deep 96-well plates overnight as primary cultures.
Inoculate 50 μL of the above saturated yeast cultures into 8 mL of SC-Ura/raffinose liquid medium in 12 channel plates until O.D. 600 reaches 1.0.
Add 2% galactose to induce expression for 6 hours at 30°C.
Harvest yeast cells by centrifugation at 3,500 x g for 5 min.
Take out yeast cell pellets from -80°C and place them on ice.
Add ~250 μl zirconia beads (0.5 mm) and 500 μl lysis buffer to each well of the yeast plate.
Cover each box with a capmat and lysate the yeast cells using the Harbil paint shaker for 2 min X 8 times with intervals of 2 min on ice.
Centrifuge cell lysates at 3,500 g for 10 min at 4°C; transfer supernatants to filter plates with prewashed 50 μl glutathione beads (GE Healthcare).
Add an additional 500 μl of lysis buffer to the yeast pellet plates and repeat step 8.
Seal the top of the filter plate tightly with adhesive foil and shake horizontally on a platform shaker at 4°C overnight.
Mix maleimide modifier modified (5') anchor oligo with anhydrous Acetonitrile.
Evaporate the mixture using a speedvac.
Re-suspend the oligo in Toluene.
Incubate at 90°C for 4 hours.
Cool to room temperature.
Evaporate toluene using a speedvac.
Take out purified TFs from -80°C and place on ice.
Dissolve lyophilized anchor oligos in PBS buffer to achieve a final concentration of 50 µM.
Add the dissolved anchor oligo to each purified protein on glutathione beads arrayed in 96-well filter plates.
Conjugate cysteine residues of proteins with maleimide group tethered to the 5’-end of the anchor oligo at room temperature for 1 hour.
Remove free oligos with three stringent washes using 50 mM HEPES pH=7.5, 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EGTA, 10% glycerol, and 0.1% beta-mercaptoethanol.
Store anchor oligo-conjugated TFs at -80°C until use.
Synthesize a collection of 2,000 address oligos containing BsaI recognition site, cutting site, UMI sequence, unique DNA barcode sequence, and consistent sequence complementary to the anchor oligo.
Prepare each address oligo in concentration of 100 µM in ddH₂O.
Use six microliters of each address oligo to prepare a 50 μl Klenow reaction mixture (1 X NEB Buffer 2 with 0.6 mM dNTP mix, 1 U Klenow [New England Biolabs], and 12 µM address oligos).
Add the 50 μl Klenow reaction mixture to the anchor oligo-conjugated TFs on glutathione beads in 96-well filter plates.
Perform the Klenow polymerase reaction at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Wash free address oligos with three washes using 50 mM HEPES buffer at pH=7.5 containing 100 mM NaCl, 1 mM EGTA, 10% glycerol, and 0.1% beta-mercaptoethanol.
Mix one fifth of the bead slurry for each protein to prepare the barcoded TF column.

Synthesize template oligos for epigenetic modified DNA libraries encoding a 5’ Primer 2 sequence (5’-CACATCCTTCACATTAATCC) with an 18-mer middle sequence containing a modified CpG, flanked by two 8-mer random sequences and including a BsaI recognition site.
Generate double-stranded DNA libraries by annealing template oligos with complementary primer oligos in a 1:1 ratio.
Proceed with the Klenow polymerase reaction according to the manual (M0210, New England Biolabs) in the presence or absence of modified dCTPs for symmetric or hemi libraries respectively.
Incubate barcoded TF columns with 200 nmole of the mixture of symmetric or hemi modification libraries in a TF binding buffer at room temperature for 30 min.
Wash protein-DNA complexes on beads three times with binding buffer and 1 X PBS buffer.
Crosslink the protein-DNA complexes on beads with 5 ml of 0.1% formaldehyde in PBS buffer for 10 min.
Centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 5 min to remove formaldehyde.
Incubate the beads with 10 ml of Tris-Glycine buffer (0.1 M glycine, pH 7.5) for 10 min to quench residual formaldehyde in the system.
Wash beads three times with tween-20 and equilibrate by T4 DNA ligase buffer.
Remove all the buffer from the beads by centrifugation at 1,000 x g for 5 min.
Add 227 µL of ddH<sub>2</sub>O with 30 μL 10 X T4 DNA ligase reaction buffer, 30 μg bovine serum albumin, 20 µL of 100 U BsaI, and 20 µL of 600 U T4 DNA ligase to the beads.
Incubate the mixture for 1 hour at 37°C.
Add 20 microliter of Proteinase K to the beads and incubate for 1 hour at 37°C.
Perform phenol/chloroform extraction on the ligated DAPPL products.
Purify the ligated DAPPL products using a QIAquick PCR Purification Kit.
Amplify the ligated DAPPL products by PCR using common primers of the libraries.
Separate all PCR products by 10% TBE gel and cut target bands with correct size.
Subject the cut bands to deep-sequencing on an Illumina NextSeq500 sequencer using a commercial kit.
